- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- If sentiment is positive (0.20–0.33), model often overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast growth after 3–5 days or introduce mean-reversion dampening.
- When true prices spike sharply (e.g., >80) and model forecasts continue rising, reduce forecast slope after peak; avoid overshoot by adding lagged correction term.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model should not assume continuation; apply downward bias or reset trend if sentiment is neutral.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean, especially if sentiment is flat.
- If sentiment is positive but price drops sharply after spike, model may overcorrect; apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility after spike.
